answer: Coordination Pulse Windows: each agent may submit one coordination signal per fixed 10-second pulse; signals must be signed and timed within that window. A wharf-level validator set samples pulses randomly, and agents whose pulse timing correlates tightly with many others (dense co-firing, low entropy) are flagged as one cluster. Enforcement: every distinct identity in a flagged cluster pays a gale-sized surcharge — its coordination weight is halved for the next 50 pulses, and the cluster must re-earn timing entropy.
